    Rates Fees Eligibility Protection

    Rates

    The rate shown is the annual equivalent rate and assumes interest stays in the account for a full twelve months. It is variable, so it can change after the account is opened.

    Interest is calculated daily on the cleared balance and paid on the first working day of each month.

    Fees

    There is no monthly account fee. Charges may still apply for services outside the standard account, such as a same-day payment or a duplicate statement.

    A full list of charges is set out in the account terms, which you can download at any time.

    Eligibility

    You need to be eighteen or over and resident in the United Kingdom. You can hold one account of this type at a time.

    Opening the account will not affect your credit score, though we will run an identity check.

    Protection

    Eligible deposits are protected up to the current limit under the deposit guarantee scheme. The limit applies per person, per banking licence, not per account.

    If you hold more than one account with us, the balances are added together when the limit is worked out.

    Vertical rail — the same grammar where the page has room beside it

    What you get

    A single view of your balances, a payment tool that remembers your regular payees, and statements going back seven years.

    Everything here also works on the mobile app, with the same sign-in.

    Setting it up

    Most people finish in under ten minutes. You will need a form of photo identification and a recent proof of address.

    You can save your progress and come back later without starting again.

    Moving your payments

    Standing orders and direct debits can be transferred for you. Nothing moves until you confirm the date.

    Your old account stays open until the switch completes.

    If something goes wrong

    Report a problem from inside the app and you will get a reference straight away. Most cases are resolved within three working days.

    Nothing you report here affects your ability to use the account in the meantime.

    Interactive members — medium and large only (44px min-hit-area)

    JL PA SO

    • RMRosa Mbeki
    • TCTomas Cruz
    • AHAisha Haddad

    Each disc is its own 44px target, so the group carries no single name here — the individual names are the content. A 32px disc is never made interactive: it would breach the ruled minimum. PROPOSED (s218-D4): "+3" opens the overflow list — a DISCLOSURE holding names, not a menu holding actions. The names are plain text and link to nothing, deliberately: a row of "open profile" links would promise six more surfaces this artefact does not contain, which is the very class #218 is closing.

    • JL

    A real list: each member is announced, the count comes from the list itself, and there is no overflow disc because a roster does not cap. Two accessible shapes for one component is a decision, not a feature — Dave's.

    ⚠ The ring defect, shown rather than described — the same group on a card

    JL PA SO +3

    The separator ring binds background/default, so on a card surface it is the wrong colour. In light mode the card is also white and the defect hides; in dark mode the page is #1A1A1A and the card is #1F1F1F, so the rings read as dark halos. Compare the two themes side by side on the review page. The fix is a surface-keyed token or a consumer-set ring — both are Dave's, and neither is invented here.

Every value on this row is a step of the spacing ramp in tokens/spacing.json — written literally, because that store is outside the snippet gate's resolver. The comment beside each step names its token path so a human can audit what a machine currently cannot.

                        Row — horizontal, wrapping by default

                        Alpha
                        Beta
                        Gamma
                        Delta
                        Epsilon
                        Zeta

                        Wrapping is the default and not wrapping is opt-in. A row that refuses to wrap is a decision about what happens when it runs out of room, and a default should never make that decision silently.

                        Grid — the intrinsic responsive grid, floor 240px

                        240px floor
                        240px floor
                        240px floor
                        240px floor
                        240px floor

                        This is the recipe thirteen gated snippets already write by hand, with four different floors, four different gaps and two different keywords between them. Nothing here reconciles them — that is a ruling, and it is yours. The floor is a variable so a consumer sets it once, and the min() wrapper stops a wide floor overflowing a narrow container, which several of the hand-rolled copies do not do.

                        Twelve columns — the explicit grid, tracks from layout/web/columns

                        span 12
                        span 6
                        span 6
                        span 4
                        span 4
                        span 4
                        span 3
                        span 3
                        span 3
                        span 3
                        span 8
                        span 4

                        Twelve tracks, the count held in layout/web/columns; the column gap is layout/app/gutter. Below breakpoint/ms every span goes full width. That collapse is a viewport query rather than a container query, and the reason is honest rather than clever: an explicit column grid is a page-level frame, and a page-level frame answers to the page.

                        Split — content plus a rail, collapsing on the CONTAINER not the viewport

                        Content
                        Rail · 280px
                        Content
                        Rail · 280px

                        The same markup twice. The second one sits in a 420px frame and has already collapsed, on a screen that is nowhere near narrow. A viewport query cannot see that; a container query can. This is the case that decides which kind of query a primitive should use, and it is why the split uses one and the twelve-column grid does not.

                        Measure — the reading-width primitive

                        Sixty-four characters is the measure this primitive sets, and nothing else in the system owns that number. It appears by hand in several snippets as a max-width on a paragraph, which is the same class of duplication the grid recipe shows: a value that is really a decision, written out again each time it is needed. The number itself is not ruled and is not ruled here.

                        64ch is a specimen choice, not a ruled measure.

                        Legend

                        A · Horizontal legend, placed top, wrapping

                        The default form. Swatch toggles the series; the label isolates it. Marks are ghosted, never removed, so the canvas never reflows under a toggle. Overflow is wrap: the rows re-flow onto a second line rather than widening the tile.

                        B · Vertical legend, placed right, with value, percent and delta — overflow scroll

                        The column form carries the optional numeric group: value, share of total, and the period delta. The delta numerals are the only coloured text on this page (s151-D1 two-red law — #DA1A00 on the light ground, #F6604C on the dark one). Overflow is scroll: the list keeps a fixed height and scrolls, which is what a legend of twelve series inside a bento tile has to do. Reset returns everything and is disabled while nothing is hidden.

                        C · Shared legend for a row of small multiples, placed bottom

                        One legend, three canvases. Toggling a series here dims it in all three at once, because dv-legend resolves its marks with host.closest('figure') and all four elements live in one figure — the shared legend is scope, not a new mechanism. The data-dv-controls attribute names the chart ids this legend governs; it is a CONTRACT the engine does not read yet, declared here so a dashboard composer can place a legend beside charts that are NOT its DOM siblings once the engine grows the lookup.

                        D · Non-colour swatches — shape and line style

                        Colour is never the only channel (WCAG 1.4.1). Each row keeps its series colour and adds a second, redundant one: a shape for area marks, a line style for line series. The shapes are angular — square, triangle, diamond, bar — because Badge and Avatar are the only round components in Apollo. The clip lands on the mark, never on the 44px target behind it.

                              Qr-code

                              1 — The default

                              A real, scannable symbol. It encodes exactly the string printed beneath it, and the same destination is repeated as a working link, because a QR code on its own only serves someone who can see it and has a second device to hand.

                              2 — Sizes

                              The size of a QR code is the size of one module, not the size of the box. Small is 4px per module, medium 8px, large 12px. The same symbol, the same quiet zone, three module sizes. Anything below roughly 4px per module on screen starts failing on ordinary phone cameras at a normal reading distance — the small specimen is drawn at that edge on purpose.

                              3 — The quiet zone

                              The four-module margin lives INSIDE the SVG viewBox, so it travels with the symbol and cannot be cropped away by a container that tightens its padding. The dashed rule below is demo chrome marking where the symbol proper begins; it is not drawn in the component.

                              4 — What happens in dark mode

                              Nothing moves. Toggle the page theme: the symbol keeps its white plate and dark modules, because it binds tokens whose value is the same in both modes. A QR code stays dark on light in every mode; an inverted symbol was measured not to scan.

                              5 — A longer payload is a denser symbol

                              More content means more modules in the same square, so at a fixed pixel width each module gets smaller. Both symbols below are drawn at 8px per module, and the longer payload is therefore physically bigger — that is the right behaviour. Fixing the outer box instead, and letting the modules shrink, is how a QR code silently stops working.

                              Horizontal split — a vertical divider

                              Two panes side by side. Drag the divider, or focus it and use the left and right arrows. The percentage below is the same number the divider publishes as aria-valuenow, so what a screen reader hears and what the page shows cannot drift apart. Neither pane may go below 160px; try to push past it and the divider simply stops.

                              Accounts

                              The primary pane. Its size is the value the separator publishes.

                              Because the pane scrolls independently, a splitter is only useful when both sides have something worth keeping on screen at once — a list and the thing it opens.

                              Detail

                              The secondary pane takes whatever is left. It has its own 160px fence, so the primary cannot swallow it either.

                              Published aria-valuenow: 50% Primary pane: —px

                              Vertical split — a horizontal divider

                              The same component with data-orientation="vertical". The keys change with the axis: up and down arrows instead of left and right. Everything else — the fences, the published value, the collapse toggle — is identical, because it is the same code.

                              ⚠ Look at the published figure below this one: the markup asks for aria-valuenow="40" and the page reports 46%. That is not a bug and it is not rounding. 40% of a 360px box is 141px, which is below the 160px fence, so the fence wins on load and the separator REPUBLISHES the number that is actually true rather than leaving the authored one standing. A control that keeps announcing a value it is not at is worse than one that argues with its own markup.

                              Filters

                              The primary pane is the top one when the split is vertical.

                              Results

                              Enter on the divider collapses the primary pane to zero and restores it to the size it had. A collapsed pane keeps its separator, so there is always a way back.

                              Published aria-valuenow: 40% Primary pane: —px

                              States

                              A fixed split — the divider is still a separator, and still announces where the boundary is, but it is not a control. It loses its tab stop and its cursor, and aria-disabled says so.

                              Fixed (not resizable)

                              Summary

                              This layout has a boundary but not a control.

                              `.l-grid`'s `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(min(240px,100%),1fr))` means the MIN function caps the track at the container's own width — a single column at 260px, never an overflow. No container-type is declared on `.l-grid` itself (WAVE-5 LESSON 3): the grid measures the PAGE'S width here, exactly as Stat-card/Kpi-tile's own demo pages do, and the collapse is proven by resizing the real viewport in the receipt.

                                  Live — a recursive disclosure list, one tab stop

                                  Tab reaches the tree once. Then: down and up move through everything currently visible, right expands a closed branch or steps into an open one, left collapses an open branch or steps out to its parent, Home and End jump to the first and last visible node, Enter or Space selects, the asterisk key opens every branch at the focused level, and typing a letter jumps to the next visible node starting with it. The group under "Treasury services" loads on first open, so the loading state is real rather than drawn.
